judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P2 (rank 1) Knowledge Objectives in Unit 1 'Numbers from 0 to 200' under the same Key Unit Competence, so grain matches and direction must rest on substantive content. The first objective is reading and writing numbers up to 200 in numerals and words (LCs: 'Read numbers up to 200 in numerals and words', 'Write numbers up to 200 in numerals and words'); the second requires showing and explaining the place value of each digit in 3-digit numbers (LC: 'Show and explain the place value of each digit in numbers composed of 3 digits'). Fluent reading/writing of multi-digit numerals and their word forms is the notational competence on which explaining the positional value of each digit depends, so proficiency in the first supports success in the second — a substantive conceptual deepening from notation to positional structure, not mere wording overlap (shared tokens were only generic: 'and', 'in', 'numbers', 'the'). Audit context confirms these are distinct printed objectives from the same table row, not duplicate extractions; both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), which limits but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P3 (rank 2) Skills Objectives in Unit 9 'Time measurement' under the same Key Unit Competence, so the grain and coordinate match and no lower-to-higher rank direction is available. 'Read the date on the calendar' concerns reading calendar units (dates, days, months), while 'Estimate time in hours' concerns approximating durations in hours; the shared LC tag is only the broad token 'time' and text overlap is negligible (jaccard 0.036). Neither skill is evidenced as supporting success in the other — calendar date reading is not a stated basis for hour estimation, and vice versa — so buildsTowards in either direction is unsupported at equal rank. They do, however, form complementary components of the same unit's time-measurement repertoire (calendar-based units alongside clock/duration units) serving the same Key Unit Competence, which supports symmetric conceptual coherence rather than dependency. First is computational ('Add and subtract numbers whose the sum and the first term do not exceed 99'); second is a concrete quantity-handling skill ('Group various objects whose numbers does not exceed 99', LC tagged counting/grouping/objects). They cohere substantively as complementary concrete-representation and operation skills over the same 0-99 whole-number range, reinforcing each other. However, the bounded evidence gives no pair-specific statement that grouping objects is developmentally sequenced into two-digit addition/subtraction (no place-value/tens-grouping language in the second statement itself), and both sit as sibling bullets in adjacent table rows of the same Skills column; same-rank directionality would rest only on source row order and shared LC tokens ('numbers', 'whole', '99'), which alone do not establish a developmental direction. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment. Note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and several ancestors are merged header organizers, so absence of further sequencing language in the excerpt is not proof of absence in the full source.
